ON SEMIPOSITIVE PIECEWISE LINEAR FUNCTIONS IN NON-ARCHIMEDEAN ANALYTIC GEOMETRY 15
![](<2503.05513_pg15_images/imageFile1.png>)
We will show ﬁrst that for an R-PL function on a smooth curve, semipositivity is the same as subharmonicity in the sense of Thuillier’s thesis [Thu05, Déﬁnition 3.1.5]. Recall that Thuillier deﬁnes a subharmonic function on a smooth k-analytic curve X as a semicontinuous function u: X → R ∪ {−∞} which is not identically −∞ on any connected component of X and which has the property that for every harmonic function h on a strictly afﬁnoid domain U of X with u|∂U ≤ h|∂U, we have u|U ≤ h.

blocks.text: We will show ﬁrst that for an R-PL function on a smooth curve, semipositivity is the same as subharmonicity in the sense of Thuillier’s thesis [Thu05, Déﬁnition 3.1.5]. Recall that Thuillier deﬁnes a subharmonic function on a smooth k-analytic curve X as a semicontinuous function u: X → R ∪ {−∞} which is not identically −∞ on any connected component of X and which has the property that for every harmonic function h on a strictly afﬁnoid domain U of X with u|∂U ≤ h|∂U, we have u|U ≤ h.

Proposition 5.1. Let X be a smooth, strictly k-analytic curve and let u: X → R be an R-PL function. Then u is subharmonic at x ∈ X in the sense of Thuillier if and only if Lu(x) is nef. Proof. First we treat the case when k is algebraically closed. As explained in 2.5, there exists a compact strictly analytic neighborhood U of x in X, a formal k◦-model U of U, and a formal model L of U such that u|U = hL. Since k is algebraically closed, we may assume that the special ﬁber Us is reduced, which implies that U is covered by formal afﬁnes of the form Spf( ◦) for a strictly k-afﬁnoid algebra [GJR21, §2.4]. It follows from [Ber90, Proposition 2.4.4] that for every irreducible component Y of Us, there is a unique point ξY ∈ U reducing to the generic point of Y. In the formalism of real valued forms and currents on Berkovich spaces [CD12], it is well known that d′d′′[u]|U is the discrete measure on U supported on the points ξY of U for Y an irreducible component of Us, with multiplicity at ξY equal to degL(Y). See [CD12, §6.9] for a more general statement. Wanner showed that subharmonicity of u on U is equivalent to the positivity of the current d′d′′[u]: see [Wan19, Theorems 1 and 2] and use the fact that X is locally algebraic [vdP80]. Thus Ls is nef if and only if u is subharmonic on U. Suppose that u is subharmonic at x. Shrinking U, we may assume that u is subharmonic on U. This implies that Ls is nef, so it follows from [GJR21, Proposition 7.1] that Lu(x) is nef. Conversely, if Lu(x) is nef, then by [GJR21, Proposition 7.1], we may shrink U so that Ls is nef, which as above implies that u is subharmonic on U.

Let k be a non-trivially valued non-Archimedean ﬁeld. We consider a good, strictly k-analytic space X. We refer to 2.5 for the deﬁnition of PL functions. Recall from the introduction that an R-PL function u: X → R is called semipositive at x ∈ X if the associated residue line bundle Lu(x) ∈ Pic(red(X, x))R is nef, where we refer to [GJR21, 6.16–6.19] for residue line bundles. Equivalently, there is a strictly afﬁnoid neighbourhood U of x such that u = hL for a formal k◦-model (U,L) of (U, U) with L nef [GJR21, Proposition 7.1].
